normalisation_variables.evidence_quote: Industry specific factors of product mix, input choice, capacity, utilization, and weather all play various roles on in inter-plant differences within the cohorts, depending on the industry in question.

baseline_construction_method.value: The approach first defines cohorts of similar plants within an industry, then uses multivariate regression inside each cohort to normalise industry-specific differences; the inter-plant benchmark can also adjust plant baselines when those conditions change.
baseline_construction_method.evidence_quote: First, a selection of “similar” plants within an industry is made.  For example, auto assembly plants were separated from engine and transmission plants.  Similarly, electric arc steel mills are separated from integrated producers in the steel industry, and pulp mills are separated from integrated paper mills.  Within these industry cohorts there may be additional variables that differentiate plants in terms of energy use, so multivariate regression is used to create a benchmark within that sub-group.

validation_types.evidence_quote: Conventional statistical tests can determine which factors to include in the model.
